subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 52-year-old man who smokes two packs of cigarettes daily tells his physician he has no intention of quitting and insists smoking has never harmed him. He cancels appointments when the topic of smoking arises and becomes defensive when his family raises it. He has made no plans to change his behavior.
question: According to the transtheoretical model of change, which stage best describes this patient?
explanation_correct: In the precontemplation stage, the individual denies that a problem exists and has no intention of changing. This patient denies harm and is defensively avoiding the topic. The appropriate motivational strategy is to encourage introspection, use the patient's own personal priorities when explaining risks, and affirm availability. This contrasts with later stages in which the person acknowledges the problem or has already committed to change.

explanation_incorrect.A: Contemplation requires acknowledging the problem but remaining ambivalent or unwilling to change; this patient denies any problem at all.
explanation_incorrect.C: Preparation involves being committed to and planning for behavior change, which is absent here.
explanation_incorrect.D: Action means actively executing a plan and demonstrating a change in behavior, not denying the problem.
explanation_incorrect.E: Maintenance means the new behavior has been sustained and integrated into lifestyle, which does not apply to this patient.

educationalObjective: In precontemplation the patient denies the problem and has no intention to change, so the clinician should encourage introspection and tie risks to the patient's own priorities.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 40-year-old woman who drinks heavily acknowledges that alcohol is damaging her health and marriage, but she says she is 'not ready' to quit and feels torn about giving it up. She has thought about reducing her drinking but has made no commitment or plan. She openly discusses both the benefits and costs of continuing to drink.
question: According to the transtheoretical model, which stage best describes this patient?
explanation_correct: In contemplation, the individual acknowledges that a problem exists but remains ambivalent or unwilling to change. This patient recognizes the harm yet is not ready to commit. The recommended strategy is to discuss the pros of changing and the cons of maintaining the current behavior and to suggest means of supporting behavior change. She has not yet entered preparation, which requires commitment and planning.

explanation_incorrect.A: Precontemplation involves denial of the problem, whereas this patient openly acknowledges the harm from alcohol.
explanation_incorrect.B: Preparation requires being committed to and actively planning for change; this patient remains ambivalent with no plan.
explanation_incorrect.C: Action involves executing a plan and demonstrating behavior change, which this patient has not started.
explanation_incorrect.E: Maintenance requires sustained new behavior integrated into lifestyle, not simply weighing the decision.

educationalObjective: In contemplation the patient acknowledges the problem but is ambivalent, so discussing the pros of change and the cons of maintaining the behavior is the appropriate strategy.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 35-year-old man who has been overweight for years tells his physician he has decided to lose weight and is committed to doing so. He has set a date to begin a structured diet and exercise program next month and asks for resources and advice on how to plan successfully. He has not yet started the program.
question: According to the transtheoretical model, which stage best describes this patient, and what is the most appropriate motivational strategy?

options.text: Preparation/determination; employ motivational interviewing and help him plan
Contemplation; discuss the pros and cons of changing
Action; focus on self-efficacy and contingency management
Maintenance; reinforce developing habits and prevent relapse

explanation_correct: In the preparation (determination) stage, the individual is committed to and planning for behavior change but has not yet executed it. This patient has decided and set a start date, matching preparation. The appropriate strategy is to employ motivational interviewing, encourage initial changes, promote expectations for positive results, and provide resources to assist in planning. Action would apply only once he begins executing the plan.

explanation_incorrect.B: Contemplation involves ambivalence without commitment; this patient has already decided and made plans.
explanation_incorrect.C: Action requires that the person is actively executing a plan and demonstrating behavior change; he has not yet started.
explanation_incorrect.D: Precontemplation is denial of the problem, which is inconsistent with his commitment and planning.
explanation_incorrect.E: Maintenance refers to sustained behavior change integrated into lifestyle, which follows action and does not apply before starting.

educationalObjective: In preparation the patient is committed and planning change, so motivational interviewing, encouragement of initial steps, and planning resources are the appropriate strategies.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 47-year-old woman quit smoking 14 months ago after years of heavy use. She no longer smokes in any situation and now identifies herself as a nonsmoker; exercise and other routines have become part of her lifestyle. At a follow-up visit she asks how to avoid returning to smoking during an upcoming stressful move. Her physician is planning the appropriate stage-based intervention.
question: According to the transtheoretical model, which stage is she in and which intervention is most appropriate?

options.text: Action; focus on self-efficacy and coping with triggers
Relapse; encourage a return to change efforts
Maintenance; reinforce developing habits, praise progress, and evaluate relapse risk
Preparation; provide resources for planning a quit date
Precontemplation; encourage introspection about the harms of smoking

explanation_correct: In maintenance, new behaviors have been sustained for more than 6 months and are integrated into personal identity and lifestyle. This woman has been abstinent for 14 months and now identifies as a nonsmoker, placing her in maintenance. The appropriate strategy is to reinforce developing habits, praise progress, and evaluate and mitigate relapse risk. She has not relapsed, so relapse-focused reassurance is not yet indicated.

explanation_incorrect.A: Action is the initial execution of a plan; her sustained 14-month abstinence places her beyond action and into maintenance.
explanation_incorrect.B: Relapse is regression to prior behavior; she continues to abstain and is proactively trying to prevent relapse, not experiencing one.
explanation_incorrect.D: Preparation involves planning for an upcoming change with a quit date; she has already achieved and sustained the change.
explanation_incorrect.E: Precontemplation is denial of the problem, which is incompatible with her long-standing successful change and identity as a nonsmoker.

educationalObjective: In maintenance, sustained behavior change beyond 6 months is integrated into identity, so reinforcing habits, praising progress, and mitigating relapse risk are the appropriate interventions.
